description: Cross-references for 47 U.S.C. § 222 CPNI and SIM swap carrier liability

cross_references.title: California Civil Code § 1798.80 et seq. — SIM Swap Protection Act
cross_references.relationship: California-specific SIM swap statute enacted 2021 that creates direct carrier liability for unauthorized SIM changes without adequate authentication. Supplements the federal § 222 framework.

cross_references.title: 18 U.S.C. § 1030 — Computer Fraud and Abuse Act
cross_references.relationship: A SIM swap that enables unauthorized access to the victim's email, banking, or device accounts triggers CFAA in addition to § 222. The SIM swap is the method; the unauthorized account access is the CFAA violation.

cross_references.title: California Penal Code § 502 — Computer Data Access and Fraud Act
cross_references.relationship: California parallel to CFAA. Unauthorized access to accounts enabled by the SIM swap violates § 502. Provides civil private right of action and criminal prosecution pathway.

cross_references.title: 18 U.S.C. § 1028 — Federal Identity Theft
cross_references.relationship: SIM swap fraud is a method of identity theft. The swapper assumes the victim's phone identity to intercept communications and take over accounts. § 1028 criminal referral is available.

cross_references.title: California Business & Professions Code § 17200 — Unfair Business Practices
cross_references.relationship: A carrier's failure to implement adequate SIM swap authentication is an unfair business practice under § 17200. UCL provides injunctive relief and restitution as civil remedies.

cross_references.title: 47 C.F.R. Part 64 — FCC CPNI Regulations
cross_references.relationship: Implementing regulations for § 222. Authentication requirements, SIM swap notification rules (2023-2024 amendments), and CPNI protection standards are in Part 64.
